reason: The quote states both routes verbatim: restore an EBS snapshot to a gateway storage volume, or, for snapshots up to 16 TiB, start a new EBS volume attached to an EC2 instance.
Under the Volume Gateways headings the quote says the point-in-time snapshots are stored in S3 as EBS snapshots and only changed data is stored for a new snapshot.
The quote states for Volume Gateways that a full upload buffer moves the volume to PASS THROUGH, new writes persist locally without immediate upload, and new snapshots cannot be taken.
The two quotes give the strong recommendation against upload buffer and cache on the same physical disk and the statement that a single-disk data store can lead to poor performance.
The first quote lists the three AZ-redundancy points for all endpoints; the second gives the single-subnet option and the multi-AZ recommendation for VPC endpoints.
The quotes state the earlier pre-signed URL REST API approach and the choice of AWS Transfer for SFTP as the alternative, described as fully managed transfer into and out of S3.
The announcement quote states access to FSx for NetApp ONTAP data over SFTP, FTPS and FTP, and the heading-scoped line gives Posted on Jan 26, 2026.
The quotes give automatic approval up to 1,000 connectors per account per Region, the default of 100, the earlier manual approval, and the Sep 30, 2026 posting date.

The document history row (September 15, 2026) states SFTP servers behind an NLB can use PROXY protocol v2 to preserve the source IP, and the What's New quote states an NLB previously replaced it with its own private IP.
The quote says to use the API Gateway option if you need a RESTful API to integrate your identity provider or want AWS WAF for geo-blocking or rate-limiting.
The quote states Transfer Family sends events to the EventBridge default event bus, which is automatically provisioned in every AWS account.
The FAQ quote gives the default domain name, Route 53 or any DNS service for a registered domain, and the internet-facing-only note on the Route 53 documentation.
The FAQ quote gives up to 5 concurrent connections, the condition that the remote server supports concurrent sessions from the same user, and parallel processing of files.
The FAQ quote states stopping by console, stop-server or StopServer does not impact billing, and hourly billing runs from endpoint creation and protocol access until deletion.
The first quote gives supported CRUD commands with files as S3 objects; the second lists directory rename, append, ownership, permission and timestamp changes and links as not supported.

The guide quote states only SFTP and FTPS on an internet-facing VPC hosted endpoint, and the FAQ quote states AS2 server endpoints support security-group allow-lists on internet-facing VPC-hosted endpoints; the claim attributes each to its page.
The quote states directories are not first-class in S3 and Transfer Family infers paths by splitting keys on the forward slash, with the last element as the file name.
The quota table row under Name, Default, Adjustable gives Maximum queue size for pending file transfers 1000, Adjustable No.
The guide quote gives up to 100 file paths per second per SFTP connector, and the General Reference row gives Rate of StartFileTransfer files per SFTP connector 100 per second, adjustable Yes.
The quote states verbatim that you can use either Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS as storage for Transfer Family servers.
The lead-in quote gives the API-access scope and the clients-must-support obligation, and the two list-item quotes give TLS 1.2 required, TLS 1.3 recommended and PFS suites such as DHE or ECDHE.

The quotes carry the VPC hosting, the three-components sentence with the first (S3 Control PrivateLink endpoint) and the third (bucket policies), but the second component, an endpoint for Amazon S3 data access, stands only in the surrounding text.
